name: Vespid Dynamics Micro-Drone Swarm Carrier MDC-1
product_name: Vespid Dynamics Micro-Drone Swarm Carrier MDC-1
description: A hip-mounted carrier that houses, charges, and deploys up to 30 micro-drones for on-demand aerial reconnaissance, communications relay, and area surveillance. The MDC-1 serves as a mobile base station for Vespid's insect-scale drone platforms, providing charging cradles, data uplink, and deployment tubes that can launch drones individually or in coordinated bursts. The carrier's AI manages swarm deployment patterns, return-to-base protocols, and battery cycling to maintain continuous aerial coverage. A single operator with an MDC-1 can establish a persistent surveillance network over a 500-meter radius.

specifications.data: Real-time video/audio feed from all active drones

story_hooks: An MDC-1 carrier was stolen along with its full drone complement — 30 micro-drones are now operating in an uncontrolled urban environment, following their last programmed orders indefinitely.
A rival manufacturer has developed a micro-drone jammer disguised as an MDC-1 carrier — it appears to deploy drones but actually emits a signal that disables all micro-drones within range.

physical_description.visual_profile: Sleek hip-mounted tactical carrier resembling a segmented insect thorax. Hexagonal modular sections stack vertically, each containing micro-drone cradles visible through translucent polymer panels. Deployment tubes protrude from the front face like a wasp's ovipositor, with articulated positioning arms. The overall silhouette is organic yet mechanical—biomimetic engineering meets corpo efficiency.
physical_description.dimensions: 28cm tall × 16cm wide × 12cm deep; fits snugly against operator's hip via reinforced magnetic mount
physical_description.weight_description: 2.8 kg loaded; worn via padded hip harness with load-distribution straps. Balanced asymmetrically to prevent torso drag during movement.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-composite chassis with reinforced titanium vertebrae; translucent polycarbonate drone cradle panels
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with iridescent oil-slick accents on panel seams; non-reflective tactical coating to minimize detection signatures
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary, electric teal accent LEDs, translucent panel insets showing neon-blue charging cradle lights
physical_description.interface_elements: Wrist-mounted neural-link receptor pad (left side), 12 tactile hex buttons for manual swarm commands, holographic micro-display (2-inch projection above hip mount showing real-time drone telemetry), 3 physical deployment tubes with motorized iris mechanisms, status indicator ring around center spine
distinctive_features: Animated LED pulse patterns along deployment tubes during active launch sequences
Visible micro-drones resting in cradles through translucent panels—tiny chrome insectoid forms with folded wings
Articulated deployment arm assembly that tracks operator hand gestures
Soft blue charging glow from internal cradle array when powered
Vespid Dynamics hexagonal logo (interlocking V shapes) stamped on left panel in brushed silver
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: VESPID DYNAMICS in angular sans-serif font; regulatory cert stamps (GLMZ Aerial Device Compliance, Swarm Authorization Class-3); serial number laser-etched on mounting bracket
physical_description.condition_typical: Active unit shows faint heat shimmer from charging cradles; occasional soft mechanical clicks during auto-cycling. Deployed unit trails microscopic drone shadows across its surface. Operator's gear typically shows scuff marks on mounting bracket and cradle dust accumulation.
